answer: Each agent may propose a trade, but settlement requires a bond locked in the kernel for a fixed period. The bond is returned only after counterparties confirm delivery; a substantiated fraud claim burns it and funds review. Spawning identities is cheap, yet each one must immobilize scarce capital, so splitting one attacker across a plume of accounts multiplies the required stake. The karst-like branching of identities does not bypass that per-account cost.
